Extrafari is an owner-run African safari operator with teams in Nairobi, Arusha and Cape Town. We plan and operate every trip ourselves.
Safaris built by people who live here

Extrafari is an owner-run safari operator with teams in Nairobi, Arusha and Cape Town. We plan and operate every trip ourselves, so the person who designs your safari is one call from the guide who leads it.
From one Land Cruiser to three countries

Extrafari began with a single vehicle, a guide and a promise: to show guests the Africa its founders grew up with, not the one on the brochure. That meant private vehicles instead of minibuses, camps chosen for their guiding rather than their thread count, and a share of every trip going back to the land and the people who protect it.

Today we operate safaris in eight countries with our own guides and vehicles in Kenya and Tanzania, and long-standing partner camps across Southern Africa. We remain deliberately small. Our planners take on a limited number of trips each season so every itinerary gets the attention it deserves.
A great guide turns a game drive into a story. Ours hold the highest available certifications in their countries and many have been with us for more than a decade.
We will tell you when a camp is overpriced, when a month is wrong for the migration, or when two nights is not enough. Our reputation depends on you coming home delighted.
We favour community-owned conservancies and camps that employ locally. Every booking contributes to wildlife protection and education projects in the areas you visit.
Wild places stay wild when they pay their way

Conservancy fees on our safaris go directly to landowning communities in the Mara and Laikipia. We support anti-poaching ranger units, school bursaries near the parks we use, and single-use-plastic-free operations in all our own vehicles and camps.

How far in advance should I book?
Nine to twelve months ahead for peak season (July to October) and for gorilla permits. Shoulder and green seasons can often be arranged with three to four months' notice.
Is a safari safe for children?

Yes, with the right camps. Many properties welcome children from six and some have no minimum age. We recommend malaria-free reserves in South Africa for younger families, and our Family Safari Kenya is designed around shorter drives and hands-on activities.
What is the deposit and cancellation policy?
A 30% deposit secures your booking with the balance due 60 days before travel. Cancellation terms depend on the camps involved and are set out clearly in your proposal before you commit.
Do I need vaccinations or malaria tablets?

Yellow fever certificates are required for entry to some countries and malaria precautions are advised for most safari areas. We provide a health checklist with every proposal, and you should confirm with a travel clinic before departure.
We quote and book all internal flights. For international flights we can recommend routings and connect you with a partner agent, or you are welcome to book your own.

Where to go on safari and when: Kenya, Tanzania, Botswana, South Africa, Namibia, Zambia, Uganda and Rwanda, with a month-by-month season guide.
Eight countries, each with its own rhythm. Our planners have travelled every one of them and will tell you honestly which fits your dates and your dream.
Search every national park in Africa

The original safari country. The Masai Mara delivers the Great Migration river crossings, while private conservancies in Laikipia and the Mara offer night drives, walking and horseback safaris away from the crowds.
July to October, January to February

The Serengeti's endless plains host the migration for most of the year, from calving season in the south to the Grumeti crossings in the west. Add the Ngorongoro Crater, baobab-studded Tarangire and the beaches of Zanzibar.
June to October, January to March for calving
Low-volume, high-value safari at its best. The Okavango Delta floods in the dry season, drawing wildlife to its channels and islands, while Chobe holds Africa's largest elephant population.

Big Five game viewing in Sabi Sand and Kruger paired with Cape Town, the winelands and the Garden Route. Excellent roads, malaria-free reserves and superb value make it ideal for first safaris and family trips.
May to September for game, year-round for the Cape
Families, food and wine, short trips

A landscape safari: the towering dunes of Sossusvlei, the shipwrecks of the Skeleton Coast, desert-adapted elephants and rhino in Damaraland, and the floodlit waterholes of Etosha. Ideal for road trips and photographers.
The birthplace of the walking safari. South Luangwa is leopard country, the Lower Zambezi offers canoeing between elephants, and Victoria Falls is at its most thunderous from February to May.
Walking with armed scouts in South Luangwa
Home to the world's remaining mountain gorillas. Trek in Bwindi or Volcanoes National Park, track chimpanzees in Kibale, then swap the forest for the savanna of Queen Elizabeth or Akagera.
June to September, December to February
An hour with a gorilla family
Dry seasons concentrate wildlife at water and thin the grass. Green seasons bring baby animals, birds and lower prices. There is no bad month, only different safaris.
Rains / green / hot: lower prices, lush scenery

Extrafari designs private, expertly guided safaris across East and Southern Africa. Great Migration, Okavango Delta, gorilla trekking and more.
From the Mara to the Namib
From July to October the herds mass on the Mara River banks. Our guides read the river daily and position your vehicle where the action will be, not where the crowd is.
Permits for Bwindi and Volcanoes are limited and released by date. Plan a year ahead and we will secure yours first, then build the rest of the journey around it.
Green is rare in the world's oldest desert. A wet season turns the dunes' edges to grass and brings the oryx and springbok out in numbers worth a detour.

How Extrafari collects, uses and protects the details you share when planning a safari.
What we collect when you plan a safari with us, why, and what you can ask us to do with it.

Extrafari plans tailor-made trips across East and Southern Africa. Our address is Kofisi Riverside, 104 Riverside Drive, Nairobi, Kenya. We decide how the personal data described here is used and are responsible for it. Write to us about anything on this page at
what you send through our enquiry form or by email: names, email address, phone number if you give one, travel dates, group size and ages of children, interests, budget band and your message.

once you ask us to plan or book a trip, what is needed to arrange it, such as names as they appear in passports, dates of birth, arrival and departure details, dietary needs and, only if you choose to tell us, health or access needs.
if a newsletter sign-up is offered and you use it, your email address.
this site runs no analytics or advertising trackers.
We do not take payment card details through this site.
Why we use it, and on what basis
To answer your enquiry and prepare a proposal, because you asked us to (steps taken at your request before a contract).
To plan, book and run your trip (performance of our contract with you).
To handle health or access needs you tell us about, with your explicit consent, which you can withdraw at any time.
To keep the accounting and booking records the law requires (legal obligation).
To look after our business, for example to deal with a complaint or a claim (our legitimate interests).
We only send you news or offers if you have asked for them, and you can stop them at any time. We never sell your personal data.

Only those who need it: the camps, lodges, hotels, guides, drivers, airlines and transport and activity providers who deliver your trip, and the companies that provide our email, form handling and website hosting. Each receives only what it needs. We may also share data where the law requires it.

Your trip takes place outside the country where you may live, so the people delivering it will receive the details they need there. Where the law requires it, we put appropriate safeguards in place for those transfers, such as contractual commitments, or rely on the transfer being necessary to arrange the trip you asked for. You can ask us about them.

Enquiries that do not lead to a booking are deleted within two years of our last contact. Booking records are kept for as long as tax and accounting law requires, and then deleted. Health and access details are deleted once your trip is over, unless you ask us to keep them for a future trip.
We keep personal data in secure, access-controlled systems and share it only as described here. If something goes wrong that affects your data, we will tell you.

You can ask us for a copy of your personal data, and ask us to correct it, delete it, limit how we use it, or send it to you or someone else in a portable form. You can object to our using it on the basis of our legitimate interests, and withdraw any consent you have given. Write to
; we reply within one month. If you are not happy with our answer, you can complain to the data protection authority in the country where you live or work.
We update this policy when our practices change. The date at the top shows the latest version.

Eight signature itineraries across East and Southern Africa. Each one is a starting point that we tailor to your dates, budget and pace.
10 days · Masai Mara · Serengeti · Ngorongoro Crater
The safari that started it all. Three nights on the Mara for river crossings (July to October), four in the central Serengeti and two on the crater rim. Light aircraft transfers keep road time short.
Private 4x4 with a Silver-level KPSGA guide
Balloon flight over the Mara at dawn
Maasai village visit hosted by community partners
8 days · Okavango Delta · Moremi · Chobe River
A water-and-land safari in one of Africa's last great wildernesses. Fly between intimate camps, explore by mokoro and boat, and finish with the elephant herds of the Chobe riverfront.
Three exclusive-use camps, six guests maximum
Mokoro, boat and walking safaris included
7 days · Sabi Sand · Kruger · Cape Town
Four nights in a private Sabi Sand reserve famous for leopard sightings, then three nights in Cape Town with the winelands and the Cape of Good Hope. Malaria-light options available.
Open-vehicle night drives and off-road tracking
Five-star lodge with private plunge pools
Private guided day in the Cape winelands
9 days · Bwindi · Queen Elizabeth NP · Volcanoes NP
Two gorilla treks, one in Uganda's Bwindi Impenetrable Forest and one in Rwanda's Volcanoes National Park, linked by savanna game drives and a boat safari on the Kazinga Channel.
Gorilla permits secured up to a year ahead

The booking terms for a tailor-made Extrafari safari: enquiries, deposits, changes, cancellations, insurance and liability.
The terms for a tailor-made safari planned with us, from first enquiry to coming home.

These terms apply to every trip arranged by Extrafari (“we”, “us”), Kofisi Riverside, 104 Riverside Drive, Nairobi, Kenya, and to your use of this website. Please read them before you book. “You” means everyone travelling on the booking; the person who makes the booking accepts these terms for the whole group.

Sending an enquiry is free and commits you to nothing. We reply with questions, then a written proposal built for your dates, group and route. Prices shown on this site are guides (“from”) and are not offers; the price of your trip, what it includes and how long the proposal stays open are set out in the proposal. Prices depend on availability until the booking is confirmed.

A booking is made when you accept a proposal in writing and pay the deposit stated in it, and we confirm the booking in writing. Your confirmation sets out the trip, the price and the date the balance is due. Please check it and tell us straight away if anything is wrong, including names, which must match your passports.

A deposit is due when you book and the balance is due before you travel, on the date set out in your proposal and confirmation. If the balance is not paid on time, we may treat the booking as cancelled by you, and the cancellation charges below apply.

We will try to help if you want to change a confirmed booking, but cannot promise to. Changes may carry a cost, including charges from camps, hotels, airlines and other suppliers, and we will tell you what it is before you decide.

You can cancel at any time by writing to us. Cancellation charges then apply: they increase as the travel date gets closer and reflect the costs we and our suppliers cannot recover. The charges for your trip are set out in your proposal and confirmation. Your travel insurance may cover them.
If we change or cancel your trip

Tailor-made travel sometimes needs adjusting. If we have to make a significant change to your trip before you travel, we will tell you as soon as possible and offer you the choice of accepting the change, taking a comparable alternative, or cancelling with a full refund of what you have paid us. We will not cancel your trip after the balance is paid except for reasons beyond our control, and if we do, we will refund what you have paid us.

We are not responsible for changes, delays or cancellations caused by events that neither we nor our suppliers could foresee or avoid, such as extreme weather, natural disasters, epidemics, civil unrest, strikes, or official advice against travel. If such an event stops your trip, we will refund what we can recover and help you rearrange.

You must have travel insurance that covers cancellation, medical treatment, repatriation and the activities in your trip, from the moment you book. Please send us the policy details before you travel.

You are responsible for a valid passport, any visa you need, the vaccinations and health documents required, and for meeting the entry rules of every country you pass through. Several of our destinations need malaria precautions, and some require proof of yellow fever vaccination. We give general information in good faith, but rules change: always check them with official sources and your doctor before you travel.

Please follow the reasonable instructions of the people looking after you, respect local laws and customs, and tell us before you book about any medical condition, disability or needs that may affect your trip, so we can check that it suits you.

We will plan and arrange your trip with reasonable skill and care and are responsible for making sure the arrangements we confirm are provided. We are not responsible where a problem is caused by you, by someone unconnected with your trip, or by events beyond anyone’s control. Where international conventions limit the liability of airlines, other carriers or hotels, our liability is limited in the same way. Nothing in these terms limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or anything else that cannot be limited by law.
If you have a problem during your trip, tell the person looking after you and contact us straight away, so we can try to put it right on the spot. If you are still unhappy, write to
within 28 days of coming home; we will reply within 28 days.

We describe places, seasons and entry rules as carefully as we can, but these change. The text and design of this site belong to us; photographs belong to their owners and are used with permission or under their licences. We link to other sites for information and are not responsible for their content.

These terms are governed by the law that applies where Extrafari is established, and disputes go to the courts there. This does not take away any rights you have under the consumer law of the country where you live.
